title: Axial Shelf Nexus: Compact workspace switcher + contextual sidebar proposal
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customers report confusion when switching workspaces and losing contextual dashboards or rollout state. The current left rail is dense and forces users to navigate multiple flyouts to reach model rollouts, cost breakdowns, and per-route dashboards. Goal: design a compact, discoverable workspace switcher that surfaces contextual navigation (dashboards, rollouts, cost views) and preserves user state during route changes. Deliver a Figma prototype, annotated decision log, and a small usability test script.
background: This ticket synthesizes prior IA audits and telemetry showing high bounce rates from dashboard pages when users change workspaces. Engineering constraints include a single-page routing model, persisted query params for rollouts, and an existing permission matrix for private deployments. We must preserve keyboard nav and ARIA semantics.
design_goals: Make workspace switching non-destructive: keep open dashboard/rollout context where possible
Surface cost and rollback affordances directly in the sidebar without adding visual clutter
Offer a collapsed axial shelf mode for tight viewports that expands on hover or keyboard focus
Ensure keyboard-first accessibility and clear feedback for cross-workspace permissions
Minimize additional API bandwidth by reusing runtime metadata and existing console endpoints
proposed_solution_summary: Introduce an Axial Shelf component: a two-state left rail that compresses to icon-only tiles and expands into a contextual nexus when activated. The nexus contains workspace switcher at top, followed by route-aware quick links: Dashboards, Rollouts, Cost Lens, Traces. Quick links load via client-side routing; if the target belongs to a different workspace we provide a non-destructive preview panel before committing the switch.
engineering_notes: Reuse /workspaces/:id/meta endpoint for name + role to avoid extra roundtrips
Client should persist query params: ?dashboard=summary&rollout_view=canary across switches when compatible
Fallback behaviour: if model/route not available in target workspace, show 'Unavailable in target' state and guidance
Performance constraint: expanded nexus must render < 120ms on warm cache (use skeletons for remote fragments)
accessibility_considerations: All interactive elements must be reachable via tab/shift-tab and have aria-labels
Collapsed mode should provide a visible focus ring and accessible tooltip with workspace name
Preview panel must be announced to screen readers when visible
Color contrast checks for new cost lens badges (WCAG AA)
tradeoffs_and_risks: Preview-on-switch adds complexity to routing and requires tight coordination with Dedicated/Private RBAC checks
Compact mode may hide discoverability for occasional users — mitigated with a first-run spotlight tour
Expanding nexus introduces more DOM nodes; may affect initial paint on low-end devices
Non-destructive switch semantics complicate analytics for 'active workspace' — require explicit events
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype covers collapsed and expanded states, workspace preview flow, and route-aware quick links
Usability test (n=8) shows 90% success on switching to a workspace while retaining dashboard context
Engineering acceptance PR adds a feature-flagged Axial Shelf component and passes perf gating (<120ms for nexus open) and automated keyboard tests
Telemetry emits events: workspace_switch_initiated, workspace_switch_previewed, workspace_switch_committed
Documentation updated in Console help center and a short in-app tour created

Annotate component behavior + accessibility in the spec doc
Run 5 quick guerrilla usability sessions and synthesize feedback
